(a) Issue a writ of certiorari or any other writ or order quashing the Preliminary Notification bearing no.BDA/ALAO/A5/18/87-88 dated 8th September 1987 published in Karnataka Gazette dated 11.02.1988 at Annexure-F by the 2nd respondent;

On 02.11.2023 following order was passed:
"Learned counsel for respondents seeks time.
From order sheet, it is seen that respondents were served in year 2014 and since then matter is being adjourned at instance of respondents.

Learned counsel for petitioner submits that decision in W.P.no.55991/2015, disposed of on 18.09.2017 would covering issue at hand as it is held therein that scheme for BTM 6th Phase has been held to have lapsed.
Under circumstances, as a final opportunity matter is adjourned to 09.11.2023 for filing statement of objections.

It is clarified that, if statement of objections is not filed by then, matter would be proceed with".
5.
Even today, learned counsel for respondents submit that they have no instructions.
In view of above, since NC: 2023:KHC:40260 granting further time would not appear to be fruitful, matter is taken up for final disposal.

6. Learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner was absolute owner of 08 guntas of land including 01 gunta of Kharab land in Sy.no.97/15 and 08 guntas in Sy.no.97/16 of Arekere - Begur Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk.
Same was notified for acquisition for BTM Layout, 6th Stage under Preliminary Notification dated 11.02.1988 and Final Notification dated 28.07.1990 as per Annexure-A.

Alleging that subsequent to said notifications, respondents have not taken possession of property nor passed award, even while petitioner continued to be in possession of land, present writ petition is filed seeking for declaration that acquisition proceedings would lapsed.

7. It was submitted that insofar as acquisition by respondents for formation of BTM Layout, 6th Stage, this Court in W.P.nos.7440-7441/2016 and connected matters disposed of on 31.01.2017 held as follows:
"2. Undisputed facts are that petitioners claim that they are the absolute owners of land bearing Sy.No.92 measuring 4 acres 28 guntas situated at Arekere village, Begur Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk.

They have executed a General Power of Attorney in favour of "Addi Housing and Industries Limited" for the purpose NC:
2023:KHC:40260 of developing the property in question and authorizing to initiate legal proceedings on their behalf.

It is, therefore, claimed that by virtue of an order passed by the Land Tribunal granting occupancy rights in favour of first petitioner and late Sri.Krishna Reddy, all the petitioners have become occupants and eventually the absolute owners of the land in question.

They have relied on Form No.10 granted C. Krishna Reddy vs State Of Karnataka on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26979041/
3 bythe Land Tribunal conferring rights in favour of late Sri.Krishna Reddy and their names have been entered in the revenue records and at the time when the notification was issued proposing to acquire the land, names of the first petitioner and late Sri.Krishna Reddy were shown as notified Khathedars and Anubhavadars.

sentences.text: Even in the final notification also names of Sri.Thayappa Reddy and Sri.Krishna Reddy have been shown as notified Khathedars.
3. The land was proposed to be acquired by the State Government at the instance of Bangalore Development Authority for formation of BTM 6th Stage.

The contention now urged by the learned counsel for petitioners is that though final notification acquiring land was issued way back on 28.07.1990, the Bangalore Development Authority has not proceeded with the acquisition in as much as it has neither passed any award nor paid compensation or taken possession of the land.

It is thus,
contended that acquisition proceedings so far as the land in question have been abandoned by the Bangalore Development Authority and State Government and therefore a declaration in this regard may be issued.
4. The Bangalore Development Authority has filed statement of objections.
There is nothing to show that award has been passed, or possession of the land has been taken or for that matter compensation payable has been paid or deposited.

The only contention urged on behalf of the Bangalore Development Authority by the learned counsel is that the writ petitions are liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches as petitioners have approached this court making a grievance regarding final notification issued way NC: 2023:KHC:40260 back in the year 1990.
He also points out that petitions are filed through a power of attorney holder - a builder.
State Government has not filed any statement of objections.
5. Upon hearing the learned counsel for all the parties, it emerges that BDA has not proceeded with the acquisition proceedings.
It has kept quiet without passing any award.
Nor has it taken possession or paid compensation to the petitioners/land losers.
Therefore, it is apparent that the land has not been utilized by the Bangalore Development Authority.

Petitioners who are the owners of the land have not lost their rights over the land in as much as they have not been divested of their rights over the land by completing the acquisition proceedings in accordance with law.

6. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for petitioners, the Bangalore Development Authority having notified the lands for acquisition and issued final declaration stating that the land was required and meant for forming a layout has not made use of the same for formation of the layout.

Though the counsel has contended that the scheme itself has lapsed because only a small portion of the land acquired has been utilized for the formation of the layout and has placed reliance on the Judgment of this court in W.P.No.27155/2014 disposed of on 06.04.2016 in this regard, it is unnecessary to deal with this aspect of the matter in the absence of proper pleadings in this regard.

However, fact remains that the acquisition C. Krishna Reddy vs State Of Karnataka on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26979041/
4 proceedings have been abandoned by the Bangalore Development Authority by not passing any award and not taking over possession of the same by paying compensation even after lapse of nearly 26 years from the date of issuance of final notification.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court and as also this court have, in number of cases, held that where the acquiring body does not take possession of the land and pay compensation within a reasonable period by discharging its duties in a reasonable NC: 2023:KHC:40260 manner, the acquisition proceedings stand lapsed.
It is well established that a power conferred on a statutory authority has to be exercised in a reasonable manner.
Exercise of power in a reasonable manner includes exercising the same within a reasonable period.

In the instant case the statutory body namely Bangalore Development Authority for whose benefit the land has been acquired was required to act in a reasonable manner within a reasonable period by passing an award and paying compensation to the land losers, and in taking over possession of the same for utilizing the land for the purpose for which it was acquired.
In all these respects the Bangalore Development Authority has failed to exercise its power in a reasonable manner or within a reasonable period.

In such circumstances as held by this court in the case of Smt.Andalamma v. State of Karnataka and Others - MANU/KA/0401/202 : 2002 (4) KCCR 2361 and H.N.Shivanna and Others v. The State of Karnataka,
Department of Industries and Commerce, Bangalore and Another - MANU/KA/2425/2012 : 2013 (4) KCCR 2793 and in the unreported Judgment dated 16.12.2016 in the case of Smt.Vajramma and Others Vs State of Karnataka and Others in W.P.No.20209/2014, the entire acquisition proceedings have to be declared as having been abandoned and consequently lapsed.

disposed of on 06.04.2016 which are also in respect of BTM Layout, 6th Stage it is held that acquisition stood lapsed.

10. In fact Annexure-G, information secured under Right to Information Act, 2005, from respondents would indicate that no award is passed in respect of petitioner's land.
